ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 2, two objects with masses m1 and m2 respectively, and m1<m2, move the same distance along the horizontal direction under the action of two forces F1 and F2 of equal magnitude. If the work done by F1 is W1 and the work done by F2 is W2, then what is the relationship between W1 and W2?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is object m2 placed on a horizontal plane, acted on by force F2; F2 is obliquely downward to the right, and the angle with the horizontal direction is marked as θ; on the right side is object m1, acted on by force F1; F1 is obliquely upward to the right, and the angle with the horizontal direction is also marked as θ. Both objects undergo displacement along the horizontal plane. Then reason: work is related only to the component of the force in the direction of displacement. The stem gives |F1|=|F2|, and the two objects move the same distance along the horizontal direction; from the figure it can be seen that the angles between F1, F2 and the horizontal displacement direction are the same, both θ. Therefore W1=F1 s cosθ, W2=F2 s cosθ. Since F1=F2 and s is the same, W1=W2. m1<m2 does not affect the magnitudes of the work done on the objects by these two forces.
